line: The Direct East Ridge follows the east ridge over a small summit to the glacier and the main summit with a 5.4 step; the Southeast Glaciers standard is the glacier/Class 3-4 route reached from Luna Pass/Col.
evidence: https://www.summitpost.org/mount-fury/152299 — lists 'East Ridge Direct' as 5.4 with about 20 ft of low fifth class rock as the more direct alternative to the glacier/traverse route
https://www.mountainproject.com/forum/message/111899304 — poster says the 5.4 exposed step route is now called East Ridge Direct
https://summitpost.org/mount-fury/climbers-log/152299 — log says the 1976 Direct East Ridge was later recognised as an entirely separate route
NOTE: the Mountain Project page 'Direct East Ridge' (106364956) is Devil's Thumb, Alaska - not this peak

line: No source found describing Sean's Route/Second Wind or an Inner Constance Northwest Buttress; the two grades (5.0 vs 5.8+) suggest different lines or a variation, but nothing confirms it.
evidence: https://publications.americanalpineclub.org/articles/12196347702 — only Inner Constance Pinnacles on a NW spur, no route names matching
Searches for 'Sean's Route' and 'Second Wind' on Inner Constance returned nothing relevant (Second Wind hit is an unrelated Snoqualmie sport route)

line: Fisher Chimneys is a 4th-class gully/ledge line to the Winnie Glacier that joins the Sulphide route on the summit pyramid; the SE Ridge (SE Corner) is a separate six-pitch 5.3 rock ridge to the pyramid.
evidence: https://mountaineers.org/activities/routes-places/mt-shuksan-fisher-chimneys — Fisher Chimneys is mixed glacier plus 4th-class scramble joining the Sulphide route
https://www.mountainproject.com/area/122727462/main-peak?print=1 — Mountain Project lists Fisher Chimneys and Southeast Ridge (SE Corner, 6 pitches, 5.3) as separate routes

line: Northwest Couloir (5-pitch ice/snow on the north-west side) and SW Couloir and Face (WI2-3 trad/ice) are separate Mountain Project entries on opposite aspects.
evidence: https://www.mountainproject.com/area/122727462/main-peak?print=1 — both listed separately, Northwest Couloir AI2-3 5 pitches, SW Couloir and Face 5.2 WI2-3

line: Mountain Project's Shuksan list has no Hanging Glacier route (only North Face); the Hanging Glacier row (5.6) cannot be matched to any source, and the North Face is the AI2-3 route; no evidence they are the same.
evidence: https://www.mountainproject.com/area/122727462/main-peak?print=1 — Hanging Glacier absent from the 11-route list; North Face listed AI2-3
Beckey's Shuksan routes mention a North Face distinct from Price Glacier; no source tying Hanging Glacier to it was found

line: The standard scramble goes up the south side to the summit block and traverses/keeps right of the southwest gully to the summit, so the stub 'South Route' (and probably 'South Face') are likely aliases of it, but this could not be proven from sources.
evidence: https://www.mountaineers.org/activities/routes-places/hibox-mountain — standard follows boot path to south side of summit block, keep right, avoiding the southwest gully
https://summitpost.org/hibox-mountain/climbers-log/153409 — a log calls the South Route a neat scramble
https://www.summitpost.org/southwest-route/163116 — SummitPost names the standard line 'Southwest Route'
Could not retrieve Beckey's own name for it; no source describes a named East Route

line: A Southeast Ridge is climbed via the Tom Cushing approach past Lobox as a separate scramble; Southeast Shoulder may be the lower part of it, but no source confirms.
evidence: https://www.mountaineers.org/activities/trip-reports/alpine-scramble-hibox-mountain-6 — Tom Cushing approach along Lobox flank then Hibox southeast ridge, descending the standard route, so the ridge is distinct from the standard

line: The stored south_route is a West Ridge scramble from Chetwoot Lake; the separate 'South Route' Class 3 stub plausibly is the same Chetwoot Lake approach but no source labels it so.
evidence: https://www.wta.org/go-hiking/trip-reports/trip_report-2021-08-31-5205858561 — Iron Cap summit reached by class 3-4 scramble in cross-country traverse

No source found naming a South Route or a Northeast Shoulder for Iron Cap; the SummitPost 'Northeast Shoulder' hit is a Utah peak (irrelevant). Northeast Shoulder treated as unknown, not shown to be same.

line: Mount Price (Middle Fork Snoqualmie, WA, 5,587 ft) has documented Hester Lake (Class 3, via saddle NW of Little Hester Lake), Northwest and Southeast routes; Lower Ramp and Prominent Dihedral (5.8/5.10) match no source and may belong to a different Price or be mislabeled; Northeast Route may be Hester Lake (Hester Lake is on the NE side).
evidence: https://www.mountaineers.org/activities/routes-places/mount-price — Price routes: Hester Lake, Northwest, Southeast
https://www.summitpost.org/hester-lake-route/163230 — Hester Lake route
https://www.yellowleaf.org/scramble/g/r/2013-10-24-mt-price.html — Price via Hester Lake
https://www.mountaineers.org/activities/routes-places/mount-price/images — gully above Price Lake northeast side as an option
No source found for Lower Ramp or Prominent Dihedral

line: The standard route is called the Southwest Ridge in Wikipedia/SummitPost and is the same climb as the stored Southeast Slopes (from Luna Col, class 2-3 to the false south summit) in all likelihood, but sources do not use the name Southeast Slopes.
evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luna_Peak_(Washington) — Southwest Ridge is the standard route, class 3/4
https://www.summitpost.org/luna-peak/151781 — from Luna Col climb broad ridge on class 2 talus 1,100 ft to the false south summit (search excerpt)
https://summitpost.org/luna-pass-sw-ridge/158668 — SummitPost page 'Luna Pass SW Ridge'
